title: UPSC CSAT Paper II — Hard Simulation 3

rubric.reasoning_layers: At least two linked deductions, constraints or conditional checks in every non-trivial item.
rubric.distractor_quality: All four options are plausible, distinct and comparable in visible length and specificity.
rubric.time_pressure: Complete paper: 80 questions in 120 minutes; revision drill: 40 questions in 75 minutes.

rubric.verification: Every keyed answer is recomputed or independently constraint-checked before PDF generation.

questions.text: The central contention developed in Passage 1 is that: Use the municipal works map as the complete information set for this question.
options: That community-based forest governance can be solved through one nationwide institutional reform under all conditions.
That community-based forest governance should be left to spontaneous private action without accountable public oversight.
That community-based forest governance is mainly technical and therefore has no significant distributive consequences.
That community-based forest governance requires aligned incentives, evidence and local feedback rather than one universal prescription.
questions.solution: The passage links the issue to incentives, evidence and feedback; the alternatives are absolute or narrowly framed.

questions.text: Reading Passage 1 closely, which inference is justified? Use the clinic-referral diary as the complete information set for this question.
options: A locally successful intervention will work identically elsewhere without any adaptation or review.
Measurement adds little when an intervention has a persuasive and desirable objective.
An intervention may fail despite a desirable objective when its feedback loop remains weak.
Administrative discretion is always harmful, even when evidence reveals local constraints.
questions.solution: The passage distinguishes a desirable objective from the quality of its feedback loop; it rejects universal claims.

questions.text: Passage 1 would be weakened most directly if which assumption failed? Use the market-access survey as the complete information set for this question.
options: Local actors always possess complete information before implementation begins.
Central rules are never useful, even when they protect minimum entitlements.
Institutional learning can improve policy without requiring perfect foresight at the outset.

questions.solution: The argument depends on learning through feedback; it does not require perfect information or reject all central rules.

questions.text: If r is the remainder when 4^23 + 5^21 is divided by 12, what is r? Use the hill-health register as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Compute powers modulo 12; cyclic reduction gives remainder 9.

questions.text: How many integers from 3 through 92, inclusive, are divisible by 7 or 17, but not by both? Use the ration audit as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Count multiples of 7 and 17, then remove twice the common multiples: the exclusive count is 18.

questions.text: Solution A contains 26% solute and solution B contains 16% solute. If A and B are mixed in the volume ratio 8:1, what is the resulting concentration? Use the tank-restoration file as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Use a weighted average: (8×26+16)/(8+1) = 24.89%.

questions.text: Three independent teams complete a task in 12, 19 and 35 days respectively. Working together at constant rates, how many days are required? Use the hostel attendance sheet as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Combined rate = 1/12+1/19+1/35; reciprocal = 6.08 days.

questions.text: The average score of 19 candidates is 54. One score of 47 is replaced by 67. What is the new average? Use the river-route log as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Change in average = (new−old)/19; new average = 55.05.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G sit in a row. C is third from the left; A is left of D; B and F are non-adjacent; G is not at an end. Which person cannot occupy fifth position? Use the border-connectivity map as the complete information set for this question.
options: A
C
D
B
questions.solution: Enumerating all valid arrangements gives possible fifth-position occupants ['A', 'B', 'D', 'E', 'F', 'G']; C never appears there.

questions.text: Six candidates P, Q, R, S, T and U are ranked first to sixth. P is above R, R above U, S above R, Q below S, and T is not first. Which candidate cannot be third? Use the vending-permit register as the complete information set for this question.
options: U
R
Q
P
questions.solution: Testing all rankings gives possible third-place candidates ['P', 'Q', 'R', 'S', 'T']; U violates the partial-order constraints in every valid ranking.

questions.solution: Y contains X plus Y-only members: 4+6 = 10.

questions.text: A field worker moves 6 km east and then 6 km north. What is the straight-line distance from the starting point, ignoring the path taken? Use the school-recovery ledger as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Displacement = sqrt(6²+6²) = 8.49 km.

questions.text: M is the sister of N. N is the father of P. P is the daughter of Q. Relative to P, what is M? Use the municipal works map as the complete information set for this question.
options: P's maternal aunt
P's paternal cousin
P's grandmother
P's paternal aunt
questions.solution: N is P's father; M is N's sister, so M is P's paternal aunt.

questions.text: Exactly one of A, B and C is guilty and exactly one statement is true. A says B is guilty; B says A and C are innocent; C says B is innocent. Who is guilty? Use the clinic-referral diary as the complete information set for this question.
options: B only
No one
C only
A only
questions.solution: Assume exactly one of A, B and C is guilty and exactly one statement is true. A says B is guilty; B says A and C are innocent; C says B is innocent. Testing A, B and C in turn leaves only B guilty: A and C are then false, while B is true.

questions.text: In a border village, a file concerning mobile-network access is being reviewed by service administrators; the available evidence includes coverage and complaint logs. A new digital process excludes some intended users. What should the officer do first? Use the municipal works map as the complete information set for this question.
options: Cancel the process and restore the former manual arrangement for every applicant.
Ask users to arrange private help while leaving the official process unchanged.
Retain the process, add assisted access and an auditable fallback, then review evidence.
Require universal digital use so that one procedure applies to every applicant.
questions.solution: The response preserves useful innovation while removing exclusion through assisted access, fallback and review.

questions.text: In a border village, a file concerning mobile-network access is being reviewed by service administrators; the available evidence includes coverage and complaint logs. options: Choose the record from the agency with the larger budget and proceed immediately.
Publish both records as equally reliable and begin implementation without reconciliation.
Postpone the intervention indefinitely until the agencies reach an informal agreement.
Create a shared evidence set, record assumptions and commission a rapid joint verification.
questions.solution: A shared evidence base and explicit assumptions address disagreement without arbitrary choice or paralysis.

questions.text: In a border village, a file concerning mobile-network access is being reviewed by service administrators; the available evidence includes coverage and complaint logs. A service reports high activity, but users say their underlying problems remain unresolved. Which measure should follow? Count total interactions without classification so that the headline number remains comparable.
Track resolution by issue type and verify a sample through independent follow-up calls.
Track average interaction time without separating issues or checking final outcomes.
questions.solution: Outcome-by-issue plus verified follow-up distinguishes visible activity from effective service delivery.

questions.text: In a border village, a file concerning mobile-network access is being reviewed by service administrators; the available evidence includes coverage and complaint logs. Reject the bid automatically because any clerical error establishes bad faith.

questions.solution: Consistent use of a pre-published rule protects equal treatment, transparency and auditability.

questions.solution: Triangulation tests measurement and lived experience before a consequential administrative action.

questions.text: In a border village, a file concerning mobile-network access is being reviewed by service administrators; the available evidence includes coverage and complaint logs. A public message must announce an uncertain hazard. Which communication is most responsible? Use the ration audit as the complete information set for this question.
options: Wait until every uncertainty disappears before communicating with the affected public.
Offer absolute reassurance so that uncertainty does not increase public anxiety.
Release raw technical figures without an instruction that people can follow.

questions.solution: Responsible risk communication is candid about uncertainty while giving a clear time-bound action.

questions.text: In a border village, a file concerning mobile-network access is being reviewed by service administrators; the available evidence includes coverage and complaint logs. Scarce services must be allocated between a larger population and a higher untreated-need rate. What rule is soundest? Use the tank-restoration file as the complete information set for this question.
options: Use untreated-need rate alone because severity should always override the population base.
Use population alone because scale is the only indicator that can be compared.
Rotate resources randomly so that no indicator receives an explicit priority.
Use a transparent composite rule weighting scale, severity and access barriers.
questions.solution: A transparent composite rule recognises scale and severity while making trade-offs reviewable.

questions.text: In a border village, a file concerning mobile-network access is being reviewed by service administrators; the available evidence includes coverage and complaint logs. A performance target encourages staff to close cases without resolving them. What correction is best? Use the hostel attendance sheet as the complete information set for this question.
options: Pair closure with verified resolution and sample audits, then revise the incentive.
Punish the last staff member who closed a case without changing the target design.
Abolish measurement entirely because every indicator creates some risk of gaming.
Raise the target further so that staff complete cases at a faster average rate.
questions.solution: The indicator must track intended outcomes and be protected against gaming through verification.

questions.text: In a border village, a file concerning mobile-network access is being reviewed by service administrators; the available evidence includes coverage and complaint logs. A vocal association claims to represent everyone, but consultation attendance is narrow. What should follow? Use the river-route log as the complete information set for this question.
options: Accept the claim because an organised association is presumed to represent all residents.
Record its view and widen outreach through accessible channels before concluding.
Decide only by the loudest vote among participants already present in the room.
Exclude the association from later consultations because its claim cannot be trusted.
questions.solution: The process respects the association's input without mistaking it for complete representation.

questions.text: In a border village, a file concerning mobile-network access is being reviewed by service administrators; the available evidence includes coverage and complaint logs. A pilot produces mixed results across neighbourhoods. How should the administrator respond? Use the border-connectivity map as the complete information set for this question.

Scale it everywhere immediately because any positive result proves universal effectiveness.
Examine context-specific results, adapt the design and publish the decision rule.
Hide the mixed results until a later evaluation produces a simpler narrative.
questions.solution: Disaggregated evidence supports adaptation rather than premature scaling, cancellation or concealment.

questions.text: In a border village, a file concerning mobile-network access is being reviewed by service administrators; the available evidence includes coverage and complaint logs. Check accessibility, repeat-use patterns and independent feedback before judging the change.
Stop monitoring because the lower number already provides a sufficient success signal.
Conclude that service quality improved because fewer complaints always mean fewer problems.
questions.solution: Complaint counts need accessibility and independent-feedback checks before they can indicate improvement.

Assess the risk, apply the documented change-control rule and retain a safe alternative.
